questions.q: In 'The Dog in the Manger', why did the Cattle call the Dog selfish?
choices: He could not eat the hay but would not let them
He ate all of their hay while they were working
He stole the meat and bones from their stalls
He barked all night and would not let them sleep
questions.evidence: He cannot eat the hay and yet he will not let us eat it

questions.q: What is the lesson of 'The Dog in the Manger'?
choices: Do not keep from others what you cannot enjoy yourself
Dogs should always sleep in the house, not the barn
Always work hard in the field before you rest
Farmers are always fair to every one of the animals in the barn
questions.evidence: Do not grudge others what you cannot enjoy yourself.

questions.q: In 'The Wolf and the Goat', why did the Wolf really want the Goat to come down?
choices: So he could eat her
So she would be safe
So she could eat grass
So they could be friends
questions.evidence: It's your own appetite you are thinking of, not mine!

questions.q: In 'The Ass and the Grasshoppers', what did the Grasshoppers tell the Ass gave them their beautiful voices?
choices: The dew they drink
Special clover
Divine nectar
Morning songs
questions.evidence: it is the dew we drink!

questions.q: In 'The Mule', how did the Mule feel after being put back into harness to work?
choices: Downhearted, and sure his father was an Ass
Proud, and sure his father was a famous racer
Happy and glad to be working again
Angry at the farmer who owned him
questions.evidence: "I was mistaken," he said. "My father was an Ass after all."

questions.q: In 'The Fox and the Goat', how did the Fox get out of the well?
choices: He jumped on the Goat's back and leaped off its horns
He climbed up the rope that hung down into the well
The farmer heard him barking and pulled him out
He dug a tunnel through the side of the well
questions.evidence: leaped from the tip of the Goat's horns out of the well

questions.q: What is the lesson of 'The Fox and the Goat'?
choices: Look before you leap
Always share your water
Foxes are good friends
Never drink from a well

questions.q: In 'The Cat, the Cock, and the Young Mouse', who was the 'fearful monster' the young Mouse saw?
choices: The Barnyard Cock
The Cat
A big barn Dog
The old farmer
questions.evidence: It was nobody but the Barnyard Cock

questions.q: What did the Mother Mouse teach her son in 'The Cat, the Cock, and the Young Mouse'?
choices: Never judge others by their looks
Always stay at home near your mother
Birds with red combs are dangerous to mice
Make friends with soft and gentle creatures
questions.evidence: never judge people by their looks
